rows.subtype: Cheering and chanting at school events [Expressing]
rows.description: A child in a sports crowd chants team slogans and claps in rhythm, feeling excitement, pride and unity. Group energy is fun but can turn to mockery of others, so children learn where cheering ends.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, excitement, pride

rows.description: A child looks up to a teacher, older sibling or sports star, copying their style and praising them. Admiration motivates growth, and it needs balance so that heroes are not treated as flawless.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration

rows.description: A school-age child says thank you, writes a note or returns a favour, feeling thankful for help or kindness. Real gratitude is more than a rote phrase, and children learn it when they see effort behind a gift.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: gratitude

rows.subtype: Joyful, delighted and amused at school age [Interpreting]
rows.description: A child learns to tell shouting excitement from teasing laughter and to check whether a laugh includes everyone. Laughing with someone is connection, while laughing at someone can wound.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, amusement, excitement, hurt

rows.description: A school-age child grieving a grandparent may cry, ask repeated questions, play normally, then suddenly withdraw. Children grieve in bursts, and steady routines with honest answers protect them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, grief, detachment

rows.description: A pre-teen who loses a best friend to a fight or a move may feel deep hurt, lose appetite or avoid school. The pain is real even if the cause seems small, and listening comes before fixing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hurt

rows.subtype: Sad, tearful and pained at school age [Regulating]
rows.description: A child learns to cry in private, breathe slowly or tell a trusted adult about hurt. Hiding sadness always is unhelpful, and long low mood with lost interest deserves adult attention.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, interest, trust, relief from stress

rows.description: A school-age child crosses arms, says no or ignores a rule to test limits and show independence. Defiance can hide fear or unfairness, so firm, respectful limits with a reason work best.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, hostility, fear

rows.description: A child wrinkles the nose and says yuck at smells, food or unfair acts. Disgust guards against contamination, but aimed at people it becomes exclusion, so kindness must be taught.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: disgust

rows.subtype: Hostile and furious in bullying situations [Interpreting]
rows.description: A child learns to spot glaring, threats, tight fists and a raised voice as signs of possible danger. The safe reaction is to move away, stay with others and tell a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, hostility, trust
